title: Order Samurai Attack Path Correlation Table
description: Declarative source of truth for execution/attack_path_correlator.py. merge_premium_findings() (and the plain static scan) already correlate findings by file/line proximity -- this table defines attack paths that correlate by MEANING instead: a fixed set of legs that, found TOGETHER anywhere in one audit, are materially worse than either alone. Structurally modeled on state/kill_chain_taxonomy.json's flat, self-describing shape (id/name/status), adapted for repo-audit findings instead of runtime telemetry events -- the two taxonomies are deliberately separate and not merged, since one classifies AGENT behavior and this one classifies CODE-level finding combinations.

escalated_severity.description: The severity of the CORRELATED finding this path produces -- independent of, and not required to relate arithmetically to, its legs' individual severities.

legs.description: Every leg must be satisfied by at least one finding in the SAME audit run for this path to fire -- an attack path is never invented from a single leg.

rationale.description: Why this specific combination is materially worse together -- becomes the escalated finding's description, so it must stand alone as a real explanation, not a label.

remediation.description: Optional combined remediation distinct from either leg's own. Omit to fall back to citing each constituent finding's own remediation.

leg.description: Exactly one of detection_id (a specific execution/detections.json entry) or category (any finding of that category) -- never both, and never neither.

category.description: Matches ANY finding of this category, regardless of which specific detection produced it.
